newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds followed their German equivalents to closed sharply higher but failed to advance at the same rate in the key 10-year sector.
Dealers said trading remained subdued with interbank professionals dominant and institutions investors restricting their interest to the middle of the curve.
One trader said Dutch bonds recovered from a mid-session slump as investors reversed previous positions by switching back into bunds from U.S. Treasuries.
"People were trying to square their positions before the weekend," said one dealer.
He said stock maturing between 1998 and 2000 remained under pressure amid switching into higher yield currencies.
Despite the strong advance, he said the 10-year Bund future remained in its recent 99.15-99.85 range.
The future was 0.25 higher at 99.54 when the guilder market closed, helped by U.S. Treasuries, which dipped on U.S. August trade data before being bought back up toward highs.
"The undertone of the U.S. bond market is very good," said one dealer, who saw this as positive for the Dutch market, despite some official views that interest rates had bottomed
